newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Clan fighting kills at least 17 in Somali capital.
newsitem.headline: Clan fighting kills at least 17 in Somali capital.

text.p: At least 17 civilians were killed in south Mogadishu in a vicious outbreak of militia fighting on Friday night and early Saturday, witnesses said.
It was the heaviest toll for more than three weeks in the clashes between clan militias loyal to faction leaders Ali Hassan Osman Atto and his rival Hussein Aideed.
Most of the fighting was around the disused milk factory and the Afgoye area in the divided south of the shattered Somali capital.
Militiamen used 106mm recoilless guns, anti-aircraft missiles and 120mm and 81mm mortars.

Militia casualties were unknown but most of the 17 civilians were killed when stray artillery rounds slammed into their houses. A mortar bomb killed four people in a camp for the displaced, including a young mother.
Faction radio stations have warned people to evacuate south Mogadishu during the past two days as tension mounted.

The clashes have their genesis in the August 1 death from bullet wounds of self-styled president Mohamed Farah Aideed. Aideed's supporters blame Atto's men for the death and appointed his son Hussein, a 34-year-old former U.S. Marine, to take over.
Somali factions, including those headed by Aideed and Atto, agreed in the Kenyan capital Nairobi last month to end hostilities, remove roadblocks and enter a peace dialogue.
The verbal agreement was brokered by Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi but, like all its predecessors, collapsed within days.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow by rebels of late President Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
